assertions.name: mixed_only_cluster_count_halves_the_worst_error_at_A_le_4
assertions.source: worst |error| over T, 3He, 4He with a single deuteron anchor: C(A,n) gives 25.0051%, mixed-only gives 12.4787%. The mixed count M_n = C(A,n) - C(Z,n) - C(N,n) is forced by (Z,N) and by which two- and three-body channels nature binds (pp, nn, ppp, nnn all unbound); at A <= 4 the simplex is complete so there is no arrangement freedom and nothing is fitted.

assertions.name: mixed_only_does_not_rescue_the_A_ge_5_divergence
assertions.source: at 6Li the C(A,n) tower gives 772.95% and the mixed-only tower 712.64% — removing the pure-flavour clusters takes out only ~8% of the excess. Part 5's refutation of the full tower stands; the A >= 5 fix is geometric (Part 13 saturation), not flavour.

assertions.name: octahedral_contact_graph_has_no_four_cliques
assertions.source: K_{2,2,2} (six close-packed spheres, octahedral): 12 edges, 8 triangles, 0 4-cliques. At most four spheres can be mutually in contact in 3D and an octahedron achieves none, so the geometric cap kills every n >= 4 term outright. This is Part 13's 'A >= 5 saturates below', made concrete.

assertions.name: the_octahedral_arrangement_choice_is_worth_over_thirty_points
assertions.source: the two distinct 3p3n labelings of K_{2,2,2} give -2.504% (8/20 labelings) and 29.995% (12/20 labelings), a spread of 32.499 points. The good one is the MINORITY (8/20). Nothing derives the arrangement, so quoting its error would be member-picking.

description: t7qv's cluster count M_n(K) must count only clusters containing at least one proton and one neutron, since pp/nn/ppp/nnn are unbound. At A <= 4, where the simplex is complete and there is no arrangement freedom, this halves the worst error (25.0% -> 12.5%) on a single deuteron anchor. It does NOT rescue A >= 5, where Part 5's refutation stands and the fix is geometric -- and that geometric route still carries a 32.5-point arrangement freedom.

data.sign_structure: C(A,n) over-counts uniformly (+13.75, +25.00, +9.13); mixed-only under-counts uniformly (−12.48, −3.82, −6.60). An over-count that becomes an under-count on removing exactly the unbound channels is what a real correction looks like; the sign agreement across three isotopes carries more than the magnitude.

A_ge_5.reading: flavour removes ~8% of the excess and nothing more. Part 5's refutation stands; the fix is geometric.

octahedral_contact_graph.why_it_matters: n-clique counting caps the tower at n = 3 for six close-packed spheres, which is Part 13's saturation made concrete.
octahedral_contact_graph.warning: the attractive number here is produced by CHOOSING the arrangement, and the good one is the minority labeling. Nothing derives it. Do not carry it forward without one.

for_t7qv: M_n should be the MIXED count C(A,n) − C(Z,n) − C(N,n), not C(A,n). Unfitted, and it halves the A <= 4 worst error from 25.0% to 12.5%.
The A >= 5 gate is geometric only — flavour does not touch it. Part 5's refutation and Part 13's saturation are one open item seen from two sides.
The geometric route needs the ARRANGEMENT derived before any number from it is quotable; it currently carries 32.5 points of freedom at 6Li.
data.verdict: The cluster count M_n(K) in t7qv's geometric weight must count only mixed clusters — at least one proton and one neutron — because pp, nn, ppp and nnn are all unbound. M_n = C(A,n) − C(Z,n) − C(N,n), which is Z·N at n = 2. On a single deuteron anchor this halves the worst A <= 4 error, 25.0% -> 12.5%, with 4He at −6.60%, and flips a uniform over-count into a uniform under-count. It does not rescue A >= 5, where the divergence is geometric; and the geometric route still carries a 32.5-point arrangement freedom at 6Li whose favourable member is the minority labeling.
